subject.title: [Bug]: Fallback model does not report progress correctly during long tasks

question: Should this report be owned by the existing async fallback-notice path, or should maintainers define a broader fallback progress contract for long-running main/subagent/heartbeat work?
rationale: Current main has partial notices and telemetry, while related open PRs only cover selected async boundaries; choosing the permanent audience, de-duplication, and routing policy is a maintainer product/ownership decision rather than a safe autonomous patch choice.

options.title: Define broader progress contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broader long-task fallback progress contract and use the existing async notice PR only as one implementation slice.

options.title: Fold into async notice work
options.body: Treat the issue as covered by the existing async fallback-notice track, accepting that non-notice progress gaps will need separate follow-up reports if they remain.

options.title: Queue a narrow repair now
options.body: Attempt a focused fix from fallback-step telemetry to user-visible progress immediately, with higher risk of conflicting with the open async and cron progress PRs.

recommendation.title: Define broader progress contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broader long-task fallback progress contract and use the existing async notice PR only as one implementation slice.

likelyOwner.reason: The fallback notice contract, docs, and observability history point to this handle as the strongest routing candidate for the policy decision.
